reason: The text explicitly describes a great outcry (צַעֲקַ֥ת) of the Hebrew people concerning their grievances. The complaints are directed at the nobles and governors (חֹרִים וְסְגָנִים) who are imposing economic hardship through usury, excessive taxation, and the confiscation of property and land. Nehemiah confronts these leaders directly, asking them what they are doing in exacting usury from their brothers. The people's complaints are fundamentally about the oppressive policies and practices implemented by the leadership class.
